newsitem.title: USA: James River to use Enron energy services.
newsitem.headline: James River to use Enron energy services.

text.p: Enron Capital & Trade Resources said it formed an energy alliance with James River Corp to identify and develop solutions to the paper maker's energy-related needs at 60 manufacturing sites worldwide.

In separate agreements negotiated under the umbrella of the alliance, James River has agreed to purchase all of the energy requirements for its two towel and tissue manufacturing facilities in Halsey and Clatskanie, Oregon from the Enron Corp subsidiary for five years beginning in the year 2000.
Enron noted this agreement is contingent upon the opening of the state's retail power market for competition.
"These two power purchase agreements are an excellent example of the potential benefits to James River from the alliance with Enron," said Tom Single, director of energy procurement for James River.

"Through these agreements, we are able to achieve some immediate relief from our current electricity costs plus we have contracted to purchase electricity at what we believe will be very competitive rates in the future."
Working together, the two companies will develop a business plan to optimize James River's energy-related assets and reduce James River's total energy costs, Enron said.

While it is anticipated the two companies will work together on a wide range of activities that could include construction and optimization of assets, the application of risk management strategies, and natural gas and power supply arrangements, James River retains rights to purchase energy from parties other than Enron.
This agreement will be in effect for four years and can be extended by mutual consent of the two companies.
"Annually, James River purchases over $200 million of energy worldwide, and we believe that substantial benefits can be obtained from a strategic alliance," Single said.
"This agreement is an important step in the evolution of our energy strategy and will position us to gain a competitive cost advantage in the rapidly changing energy marketplace."

Enron believes "James River will realize significant benefits through the focused application of Enron's innovative energy and finance capabilities," said Kenneth D. Rice, chief executive of Enron Capital & Trade Resources - North America.
"Many of these benefits can be realized even prior to the opening of retail electric markets."
